$comment: Vendored conformance table for the Mermaid Gantt directives this engine implements. Read from the shipped grammar and renderer of the version below, not from prose, so a claim here can be checked against the file named in `source`. Every token this engine accepts and every token it refuses appears once; `supported:false` is a deliberate published gap, not an oversight.

provenance.note: The dateFormat token table is dayjs' customParseFormat vocabulary (moment's spelling), the axisFormat table is d3-time-format's strftime vocabulary, and the tickInterval and duration grammars are the two regular expressions the shipped chunk executes. The `excludes`, `includes` and `inclusiveEndDates` entries are read from the chunk's gantt database (`isInvalidDate`, `checkTaskDates`, `getEndDate`, `mergeTokens`) and its lexer. The `topAxis` and `displayMode` entries are read from the chunk's renderer (`makeGrid`, `getMaxIntersections`), from the lexer rule and parser action for `topAxis`, and from the front-matter step that copies a top-level `displayMode` into the gantt config. The `click` entry is read from the chunk's lexer rules, its clickStatement productions and its `setLink`, `setClickEvent` and `setClickFun` actions, and each form and reject was run through the shipped gantt database at both the default and the loose security level.

dateFormat.grammar: dayjs customParseFormat; a bracketed run is a literal

tokens.reason: the LDML fraction tokens are tenths (S) and milliseconds (SSS); there is no hundredths field to read into
a quarter is derived from a month rather than a field of a date, so the core parser refuses it

tokens.means: day of month with an ordinal suffix
tokens.reason: the suffix is locale text (1st, 1er, 1º) and this engine ships no ordinal data
derived from a date, not a field of one
derived from a date, not a field of one
an epoch is a whole value, not a calendar field; write it as a date instead
an epoch is a whole value, not a calendar field; write it as a date instead
the ISO week number is derived from a date rather than a field of one, so a parser has nothing to read it into
the ISO week number is derived from a date rather than a field of one, so a parser has nothing to read it into

tokens.computed: the year of the ISO week holding the instant, modulo 100, two digits
the year of the ISO week holding the instant, modulo 10000, four digits
the instant itself, a whole number of milliseconds
the instant in seconds, rounded down, so -1.5 s is -2

tokens.reason: the formatter pads with zeroes or not at all; a space-padded field would be a token of its own
it expands to %e, which is unsupported

tokens.means: week of the year, Sunday first
tokens.reason: the core week number is ISO (Monday first, week 1 holds January 4th) and is a different rule, so answering with it would be wrong rather than approximate

tokens.means: week of the year, Monday first
tokens.reason: d3 counts from the first Monday; ISO counts from the week holding January 4th, so the two disagree in January
the core weekday number is ISO (1 is Monday), so the same digit would mean a different day

weekday.means: which day a `tickInterval` of whole weeks starts on

weekend.means: the first of the two days `excludes weekends` removes

excludes.note: `weekends` removes the `weekend` day and the day after it; a named weekday removes every occurrence of that day; a date removes that one day. Every `excludes` line adds its terms to one list.

includes.note: A date given here is a working day whatever `excludes` says, so it wins over `weekends`, a weekday name and an excluded date alike. Every `includes` line adds its terms to one list, and the directive changes nothing while nothing is excluded. Mermaid compares each probed day with these strings only, so a weekday name, `weekends` or any other word matches no day and is ignored. A trailing `%%` comment is skipped.

inclusiveEndDates.note: An end written as a date in `dateFormat` names the last day worked, so the task ends one day after it; a duration and `until` are unchanged.

topAxis.note: The renderer draws a second axis, with the same ticks and labels, when the gantt config's `topAxis` is truthy: the string "false" turns it on. The grammar lexes a `topAxis` line but its action calls a database method that is not there, so the line itself fails with `yy.TopAxis is not a function` and the config is the only way to turn the axis on there.

displayMode.note: The renderer packs a section's tasks into rows when the gantt config's `displayMode` is exactly `compact`: tasks in start order, source order breaking ties, each into the first row whose last task has ended by its start (the effective end, after `excludes` has pushed it), so a task that starts the instant another ends shares its row. A top-level front-matter `displayMode` is copied into `config.gantt.displayMode` and wins over a `config` member there; an init directive wins over both. The lexer has no rule for a `displayMode` line, so one reads as a task row.

click.grammar: click <ids> [href "<url>"] [call <name>(<arguments>)], with at least one of the two, each at most once and in either order, then an optional `%` comment
click.ids: one word of task ids separated by commas, no spaces; an id that names no task binds nothing

rejects.reason: neither an href nor a call
a call needs a function name

rejects.source: click a1 call f() call g()

rejects.reason: href needs whitespace before its quote

click.callArguments: split at each comma with an even number of double quotes after it, each piece trimmed, one pair of surrounding quotes removed; none written is an empty list, and Mermaid then passes the task id when it runs the call

href.mermaid: the URL goes through the @braintree/sanitize-url filter unless securityLevel is loose, which turns javascript: into about:blank; the task gets the class `clickable`, and a click on its bar or its label calls window.open(url, "_self"); with securityLevel sandbox the bar and label are wrapped in an anchor
href.jaren: the URL goes through sanitizeHref, an allow-list, and is percent-encoded for the attribute; a task whose URL fails it has no link and no anchor

call.mermaid: nothing is bound unless securityLevel is loose, where the click runs the global function of that name with the arguments; the task is `clickable` either way
call.jaren: recorded in the tree as a name and its argument strings and never looked up, bound or run, whatever the config says; the task is not drawn clickable

click.order: Mermaid applies a click when the line is read, so a click written before its task, or naming an id no task has, has no effect; here a click binds by id wherever it is written, and an id no task has still binds nothing
click.note: The lexer rules are `click[\s]+`, `href[\s]+["]`, `call[\s]+`, `\([\s]*\)`, `\(` and `\)`; the productions are clickStatement 34-40 and the actions `setLink`, `setClickEvent` and `setClickFun`, all read from the chunk `provenance.source` names. A line that starts with the word and carries a task's `:` outside quotes and parentheses, such as `Click the button : a3, 2024-01-09, 1d` or `Click on href : a3, 2024-01-09, 1d`, fails Mermaid's parse and stays a task row here. `click , href "u"` names no id: Mermaid accepts it and binds nothing, and it is refused here because the printer could not write it back.

status.note: Flags lead the task data, in any order, before the id and the dates.

taskForms.note: starts where the previous task ended

divergences.what: a schedule with no dated anchor
divergences.jaren: a JM error naming the task and its line
divergences.why: no operation in this suite reads the clock, so a diagram whose meaning changes daily has no answer to give

divergences.what: an unsupported dateFormat or axisFormat token
divergences.mermaid: the token is passed through as a literal
divergences.jaren: a JM error naming the token and the reason
divergences.why: a silent literal turns a typo into a date that parses as something else

divergences.what: a task row whose name starts with includes or inclusiveEndDates (includes the API docs : a1, 2024-01-05, 3d)
divergences.mermaid: the whole line is the directive and the task is dropped
divergences.jaren: a line holding a colon that is not inside a time is a task row, as it was before the words were directives
divergences.why: a task named in plain words should not vanish, or be refused, because its first word is also a directive

divergences.mermaid: the grammar lexes it and then fails with `yy.TopAxis is not a function`
divergences.jaren: the line is kept in meta and turns the second axis on, as the config's topAxis does; anything after the word is ignored
divergences.why: the line is the directive's evident spelling, a document carrying it already rendered here, and a refusal would break it for no gain

divergences.what: an after naming an id no task has
divergences.jaren: a JM error naming the task and the id
divergences.why: the start would again depend on a clock this engine does not have, and a guessed dependency is a schedule nobody wrote

divergences.what: compact mode with two sections of the same name, or with section names that are integers
divergences.mermaid: the renderer groups the tasks by section name and walks the groups in JavaScript key order, so same-named sections pack together and an integer-looking name jumps to the front
divergences.jaren: every section packs on its own and the sections keep their source order
divergences.why: a section is a position in the document, and a name that sorts differently from where it was written would move rows away from their headings

divergences.what: a click href that is unsafe or bare-relative (javascript:, data:, page.html)
divergences.mermaid: javascript: becomes about:blank and the task is still a link; a relative URL is kept; the filter is the sanitize-url package
divergences.jaren: only the URL forms sanitizeHref allows draw a link (http and https URLs, mailto, a fragment, a protocol-relative URL, a root-relative path and a dot-relative path); any other URL leaves the task without a link, and the tree keeps the URL as written
divergences.why: the allow-list is the one policy every link in this package already goes through, and a link that goes nowhere is worse than none

divergences.mermaid: inert at the default security level, and a call of the page's global function at loose
divergences.jaren: kept in the tree as a name and argument strings and never drawn or run at any config
divergences.why: a diagram is data from an author the host may not trust, and a name in the text must never choose which function runs; a host that wants the call reads the tree and decides

divergences.what: a click written before its task, or on a line that merely starts with the word
divergences.mermaid: a click before its task has no effect, and a task row such as `Click the button : a3, 2024-01-09, 1d` fails the parse
divergences.jaren: a click binds by id wherever it is written, and a line that does not read as a click statement and carries a task's colon stays a task row
divergences.why: schedules already resolve forward references, and a task named in plain words should not be refused because its first word is a keyword
